questions.q: On which day is story time for Primary 1 and Primary 2?
questions.tip: The Monday row says P1 and P2 in the 'Who it is for' column.
Read across the Wednesday row to the Reader column.

questions.q: How long does one session last?
questions.tip: The first bullet point says each session lasts 30 minutes.

questions.q: Why does the notice tell pupils to bring a cushion?
questions.tip: The bullet point gives the reason straight after the instruction.

questions.q: A pupil wants to borrow the book that was read. When may she do it?
questions.tip: The last bullet point says 'but only after the session ends'.

Shirt$6$3

questions.q: How much would a 'good as new' shirt and a 'well worn' skirt cost together?
questions.tip: $6 for the shirt plus $2 for the well-worn skirt = $8.

questions.q: Which item cannot be bought in 'well worn' condition?
questions.tip: The Shoes row says 'not sold' in the Well worn column.

questions.q: A family buys four well-worn PE T-shirts. What do they pay?
questions.tip: 4 × $2 = $8, and four items earns the $3 discount, so $8 − $3 = $5.

questions.q: A parent brings a card to pay with. What is the problem?
Someone arrives at 11.30 a.m. with uniform to donate. What is the problem?
options: Donations are only taken until 11 a.m.
questions.tip: The last line says donations are welcome 'up to 11 a.m.'.

questions.q: Where may a pupil try something on?
options: Behind the screen at the back of the hall
questions.tip: The small print says items may be tried on behind the screen at the back.

questions.q: What happens to the money raised?
options: It goes to the school's book fund
questions.tip: The last line of the shaded box says so in bold.

questions.q: Why do you think the sale is called 'Pre-loved' rather than 'Second-hand'?
options: It makes used clothes sound cared for rather than worn out
It is the official name for uniform
It means the clothes are free
questions.tip: 'Pre-loved' is a friendlier way of describing something that belonged to somebody else.

listening5.title: Listening Comprehension · Practice Paper 5 (Primary 3–4)
listening5.instructions: An adult reads each text aloud TWICE at a normal pace, with a short pause between the two readings. The child reads the question and the four options first. Do not show the child the script. This paper is shorter and simpler than papers 1 to 4. 15 marks.

items.script: Good morning, Primary 3 and Primary 4. Please remember that tomorrow is a half day. Lessons end at eleven o'clock. The school bus will come at the usual time in the morning, but the afternoon bus will leave at quarter past eleven instead of one o'clock.
items.q: What time will the afternoon school bus leave tomorrow?
items.tip: The lessons end at eleven and the morning bus is at the usual time. The question asks about the AFTERNOON bus: 'the afternoon bus will leave at quarter past eleven instead of one o'clock'.

items.script: Girl: Have you seen my water bottle? Boy: The blue one? It was on the bench near the canteen. Girl: That was this morning. I looked there just now. Boy: Then try the lost property box. Somebody probably handed it in.
items.q: What does the boy tell the girl to do?
items.tip: She has already looked on the bench — 'I looked there just now' — so his advice is the next thing he says: 'Then try the lost property box.'

items.script: Attention, shoppers. The lift to level three is not working this afternoon. Please use the escalator next to the bakery, or the stairs beside the toilets. Our engineers hope to have the lift working again by tomorrow morning.
items.q: Which two ways can shoppers get to level three?
items.tip: The lift is the one that is NOT working. He offers two others: 'the escalator next to the bakery, or the stairs beside the toilets'.

items.script: Father: Did you feed the rabbit? Boy: Yes, this morning. Father: And the water? Boy: I changed it yesterday. Father: It needs fresh water every day, not every other day. Boy: I will do it now.
items.q: What has the boy forgotten to do today?
items.tip: He fed the rabbit this morning, so that is done. The water was changed yesterday, and the father says it needs fresh water 'every day, not every other day' — so the water is today's job.

items.script: This is a reminder about the class photograph. It will be taken on Thursday during the second period. Everybody must wear the full school uniform, including the tie. Pupils who have physical education that morning should bring their PE kit and change afterwards, not before.
items.q: When should pupils change into their PE kit?
options: They should not change at all
items.tip: 'Bring their PE kit and change afterwards, not before.' Afterwards means after the photograph.

items.script: Girl: I cannot come on Saturday after all. Boy: Why not? Girl: My grandmother is visiting from Malacca. Boy: That is a pity. Shall we go on Sunday instead? Girl: Sunday morning would work. I have swimming in the afternoon.
items.tip: Saturday is out because her grandmother is visiting. She then says 'Sunday morning would work' — the afternoon is taken by swimming.

items.script: Pupils, the drinks stall will be closed for three days next week while the machine is repaired. Please bring a water bottle from home. There is a water cooler outside the hall, and another one on the second floor near the music room.
items.q: Why will the drinks stall be closed?
items.tip: 'The drinks stall will be closed for three days next week while the machine is repaired.' Three days is how long, not why.

items.script: Boy: How far is the wetland reserve? Teacher: About forty minutes by coach. Boy: And how long will we stay? Teacher: Three hours. We leave school at eight and get back at about one o'clock.
items.q: How long will the coach journey take?
items.tip: 'About forty minutes by coach' answers the journey. Three hours is how long they stay once there.

items.script: Good afternoon. The swimming pool will open half an hour later than usual on Wednesday, at half past three, because the water is being tested. Lessons booked for three o'clock will be moved to four o'clock. Nobody needs to rebook.
items.q: What must people with a three o'clock lesson do?
options: Nothing — it moves to four o'clock
items.tip: 'Lessons booked for three o'clock will be moved to four o'clock' and then 'Nobody needs to rebook' — so there is nothing for them to do.

items.script: Girl: The recipe says two hundred grams of flour. Boy: We only have a hundred and fifty. Girl: Then we halve everything. One hundred grams of flour, one egg instead of two. Boy: And we will get half as many biscuits. Girl: Twelve instead of twenty-four.
items.q: How many biscuits will they make?
items.tip: Halving the recipe halves the biscuits, and she says the number out loud: 'Twelve instead of twenty-four.'

items.q: How long will the class look after Nibbles?
items.script:
Right, everyone, listen carefully. This is about the class pet.

From Monday we are looking after Nibbles, the school guinea pig, for four weeks.

Two of you will be on duty each day. Your names are on the chart by the door. You feed him before school, not at recess, because he eats in the morning.

He has fresh hay every single day. Fresh water every single day as well, not every other day.

Do not give him anything from your lunchbox. Not bread, not biscuits, not fruit. The only food he gets is what is in the green tub.

On Friday afternoons we clean the whole cage, which takes about twenty minutes and needs four people.

One last thing. He is quiet, and he will let you pick him up, but he does not enjoy it. Stroke him in the cage instead. A guinea pig that is handled too much stops eating, and a guinea pig that stops eating gets ill very quickly.
items.tip: 'From Monday we are looking after Nibbles… for four weeks.'
'You feed him before school, not at recess, because he eats in the morning.'

items.q: How often does he need fresh water?
items.tip: 'Fresh water every single day as well, not every other day.'

items.q: What may pupils give him from their lunchbox?
items.tip: 'Do not give him anything from your lunchbox. Not bread, not biscuits, not fruit.' Every option is named and refused, so the answer is nothing at all.

items.q: Why should pupils stroke him in the cage instead of picking him up?
options: Too much handling makes him stop eating and fall ill
items.tip: The last lines give the reason: 'A guinea pig that is handled too much stops eating, and a guinea pig that stops eating gets ill very quickly.'
